slides.title: Analysis for the Differences Between Standard Congestion Control Schemes (draft-nishida-ccwg-standard-cc-analysis)

polls.text: CCWG should work on this topic (update Reno and/or CUBIC)

chat.author: Reese Enghardt
chat.text: Slide 71 here: https://datatracker.ietf.org/meeting/127/materials/slides-127-iccrg-improving-the-evaluation-of-heterogenous-congestion-control-algorithm-interactions-00

chat.author: Christian Huitema
chat.text: Yes! It is time to retire Reno and Cubic!

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: To be clear: I am not saying the harm measurement in iccrg means we can't move forward, but the proponents should at least look at it

chat.author: Neal Cardwell
chat.text: Yes. Agreed. Thanks!

chat.author: Gorry Fairhurst
chat.text: There were good tests for a BDP of "up to 60 packets," and I note there are also paths that have a larger BDP in the Internet :-)

chat.author: Neal Cardwell
chat.text: Here's the comparison I was thinking about for various startup/slow-start approaches: https://github.com/google/bbr/blob/master/Documentation/startup/gain/analysis/bbr_startup_gain_graph.png

chat.author: Craig Taylor
chat.text: Thanks Neal

chat.author: Lucas Pardue
chat.text: nice work on ns3 integration

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: As screamv2 is going for experimental, the bar is a bit lower for rfc

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: But it would be nice to have some evaluation of harm and in non-5G networks

chat.author: Christian Huitema
chat.text: (clap)

chat.author: Ingemar Johansson
chat.text: I need to look into the ICCRG presentation again and see how harm can be evaluated with SCReAM, some kind of the cross traffic remediation is however needed to avoid that SCReAM  starved out. I think anyway that the SCReAM BW test tool can be used for this purpose.

chat.author: Ingemar Johansson
chat.text: Great work with the hackathon

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: This is so incredibly clever, and if for some reason we ever re-open cubic we should consider doing this. But I don't want to reopen Cubic

chat.author: Christian Huitema
chat.text: I wonder how many QUIC deployments actually use RFC9002.

chat.author: Kazuho Oku
chat.text: for loss recovery, they do, no?

chat.author: Christian Huitema
chat.text: for congestion control?

chat.author: Kazuho Oku
chat.text: For QUIC CC, I anticipate the same, i.e., deployments are unlikely to be using bare Reno

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: I don't think this is useful as quic vs tcp analysis because reno quic is ~zero

chat.author: Kazuho Oku
chat.text: I think the majority of the differences of QUIC being presented were loss recovery?

chat.author: Rui Paulo
chat.text: historically, TCP did not deal with packets but dealt with bytes acked.  QUIC dealt with packets acked since RFC 9001 so that's a non loss recovery difference

chat.author: Rui Paulo
chat.text: 9002, of course...

chat.author: Lars Eggert
chat.text: Who let Fluffy anywhere near CC?

chat.author: Cullen Jennings
chat.text: Send it all full speed, all the time :-)

chat.author: Giovanni Marzot
chat.text: +1 to full speed

chat.author: Ali Begen
chat.text: Take what you can, give nothing back

chat.author: Eric Kinnear
chat.text: @kazuho, it's interesting to look at CUBACK with the lens that p99-ish for web resources is around 1MB (much higher for non-web), but we also send/receive many of them in any particular page load. Did you see anything interesting from different cadences of traffic (i.e. 3MB but with gaps vs. w/o gaps)?

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: We do allow space for experimental RFCs with less than global deployment, but there needs to be a lot more simulation than this

chat.author: Reese Enghardt
chat.text: Or testbeds. Where are all those Congestion Control PhD students? :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: This WG has so many RT CCs. Does someone has a taxonomy of the pros and cons of each?
